0. FOREWORD
Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 11 February 1980, after the draft finalized by the Documentation Sectional Committee had been approved by the Executive Committee. 0.2 Microfilming is being increasingly used in archives, libraries, record offices, information centres and other academic'research institutions for making copies of articles, rare books, manuscripts, records and other information material. It is desirable to adopt a uniform practice for This arrangement and sequence of text including bibliographical details. will facilitate their use, retrieval of contents and exchange between different centres. 0.3 In the preparation of this standard, taken from the following publications: IS0 Dot: 1116-1975 Microcopying spools and reels, International considerable assistance has been

SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies sequence, order and placement of images in microfilming of records, books and other publications and also sequence It covers of bibliographical data for quick identification and retrieval. 35 mm perforated and unperforated microfilms. 16 mm and Requirements of this standard do not necessarily apply to microfilm strips.

The distance of the text or the useful part of the images from the edge of the non-perforated film and from the inner edges of perforation of the perforated film shall not be less than I.00 mm fbr 35 mm film and 0.5 mm for 16 mm film. The images shall not overlap and the distance between adjacent frames shall preferably be not less than 1'00 mm for 35 mm film and 0.5 mm for 16 mm film. Depending upon the size and characteristics of the documents may be filmed either one page or two pages frame. IS:9450-1980 7.1.2.1 Identzjkation area - This area is intended for formal identification and classification of the microfilm rolls by means of archive or library classification marks and numbers of references and inventories as shown below. This area may be left blank for use by the end users. 11'. A. I. Private Papers Tagore Collection National Library District Gazetteers u. P.

7.1.2.2 Archivographic or bibliographic area - This area is intended for document information that is archivographic or bibliographic information on the documents reproduced. This shall include the name of the country in which the documents are kept, the name of the institution or person possessing the documents, the designation of the main archive group, collection to which the documents belong, the description or title of the documents or the archive sub-group they constitute and an indication of the volume of documents. INDIA, VISHWA BHARATI, SHANTINIKETAN TAGORE DIARIES 25 MARCH 1937 to 10 DECEMBER 1940 (41 ) Examflle 2: NATIONAL INDIA, HINDU OPINION 2 APRIL 1863-5 MAY LIBRARY, 1892 (1405 ) or legal binding shall be CALCUTTA

restriction Any notice of ' copyright' microfilmed in this area in the lower part.

7.1.2.3 Sequential area - This area represents the sequential numbering of microfilms containing the documents specified in archivographic or bibliographic area.
